Description: Review last year's CFP outcomes and the last two retros for speaker-related action items
Notes: Document lessons learned before setting this year's timeline

Description: Review previous proposals and identify topic areas to encourage in CFP promotion
Notes: Feedback asks for more deep technical and design talks vs tool demos

Description: Invite tutorial presenters directly starting with hallway conversations at PyCon US
Notes: Tutorials are invited directly and are not part of the open CFP; keep a ranked shortlist with backups

Description: Launch the keynote nomination Google Form at the kickoff meeting
Notes: Form lives in the year's Drive folder under Speakers

Description: Confirm the CFP opens October 1 and closes early December with review over the holidays and notifications around the new year
Notes: 9-10 week window; October 1 open is the cycle's first hard deadline

Description: Review and update the Pretalx submission form (title abstract bio photo recording consent CoC agreement)
Notes: Include a travel-assistance question; answers feed opportunity grant planning

Description: Recruit reviewers from the committee and community and brief them on rubric and deadlines
Notes: Review and voting happen in Pretalx

Description: Define scoring criteria for relevance clarity originality feasibility and audience interest
Notes: Consistent rubric keeps review fair

Description: Draft CFP copy welcoming all levels and coordinate graphics and campaign schedule with Marketing
Notes: Newsletter goes out the 1st of the month and must link the live site

Description: Close the nomination form at end of September and compile the candidate list
Notes: Prep the organizer election ballot next

Description: Open submissions October 1 and retest the submission flow
Notes: October 1 is the institutional open date

Description: Coordinate the launch campaign: newsletter social Discord python.org events and pythondeadlin.es
Notes: Send direct invitations to the past-speaker Google Group the same day

Description: Run a ranked-ballot Google Form election among organizers scoring each candidate from +2 to -2
Notes: Compile results into a rankings doc with vote scores

Description: Decide the ordered invite list from the rankings doc as a team
Notes: Invitations often go several names deep; the ranked backup list is the plan

Description: Work down the invite list in order with clear offers and follow-up cadence
Notes: Target keynotes confirmed by Month -5; some candidates take weeks to respond

Description: Schedule reminder pushes mid-window and a countdown in the final week before close
Notes: Include Texas meetup lists in the mid-window push

Description: Track submission volume answer submitter questions and offer CFP-writing help via Discord
Notes: Expect a few dozen submissions over the 9-10 week window

Description: Close Pretalx at the deadline in early December and prepare for review
Notes: A short extension is an option if volume is low near the deadline

Description: Reviewers vote in Pretalx over at least 2 full weeks (usually across the holidays)
Notes: Monitor progress and send reminders

Description: Meet in person to pick the lineup and build an ordered waitlist with top candidates flagged
Notes: Target around 14-15 talks for the single track

Description: Send the speaker info form to accepted speakers at acceptance time to collect name socials photo and logistics
Notes: Collect this at acceptance; chasing it later is painful

Description: Draft acceptance email with confirmation deadline speaker info form link and next steps
Notes: Use the template in the runbook

Description: Write kind rejection email thanking submitters and inviting future submissions
Notes: Keep it encouraging

Description: Email acceptances around the new year with a hard confirmation deadline of about 2 weeks
Notes: MILESTONE: reject everything below the waitlist promptly

Description: Monitor confirmations promote from the ordered waitlist on declines and offer standby speakers free tickets
Notes: Late dropouts happen even after the schedule is final; hold ordered alternates

Description: Confirm all tutorial presenters and their prework or prerequisite communications
Notes: Plan on two community tutorials plus a possible sponsored workshop

Description: Build the schedule in 30-minute blocks (25-minute talk plus 5 minutes of Q&A and setup) with keynotes after opening remarks and a 20-minute sponsored talk before lunch
Notes: Coordinate lunch and breaks with Venue

Description: Coordinate with Finance to slot sponsor pitches by tier spaced across the days
Notes: Platinum pitches Saturday; Gold/Silver Sunday

Description: Present the draft schedule to the organizers for feedback and conflict checks
Notes: Also conflict-check with speakers before publishing

Description: Lock the schedule and publish it with Marketing
Notes: The PSF grant application requires a published schedule

Description: Request single-event quotes for Slido (Q&A) and StageTimer (speaker timing)
Notes: One StageTimer login is enough

Description: Work with Finance on grant review; accepted speakers requesting support get priority
Notes: Applications close about Week -8.5 with a special review meeting the next day

Description: Email speakers their confirmed slots and the published schedule link
Notes: Set expectations early

Description: Write or update the speaker guide: slot Discord role slide upload tech-check windows green room and Friday dinner
Notes: Speakers don't read emails; the KBYG is a reference not the briefing

Description: Send the KBYG about 2 weeks out
Notes: Two weeks out is the floor; earlier is better

Description: Open the shared Drive folder and ask each speaker for a text file of technical terms for caption prep
Notes: USB-C is the preferred connection; stage backup dongles (Dell Apple HP)

Description: Create per-day lightning talk signup Google Forms with 8-9 slots per day
Notes: Submissions exceed slots; organizers curate an ordered subset

Description: Confirm the speaker headcount for the Friday appreciation dinner with the Venue Committee
Notes: Dinner covers speakers sponsors organizers and Friends of PyTexas

Description: Email speakers final reminders: arrival on-deck rule tech-check windows and contacts
Notes: Last written touchpoint before the in-person briefing

Description: Offer speaker tech checks Friday before 9:00 or at lunch
Notes: Weekend checks are catch-as-catch-can between stage events

Description: Welcome instructors and verify room setup before each session
Notes: Power strips at every table

Description: Brief speakers in person at the Friday appreciation dinner
Notes: Speakers don't read emails; this is the real briefing

Description: Coordinate with Venue on location and stock with water snacks power and seating
Notes: Check the green room before each talk block

Description: Place the table near the stage with clear signage and backup dongles ready
Notes: The on-deck rule keeps the conference on schedule

Description: Welcome each speaker and walk through slot mic timer and the on-deck rule
Notes: Track arrivals against the schedule

Description: Seat the next speaker when the prior talk begins and tech check during the 5-minute changeover
Notes: The most important speaker coordination process

Description: Handle laptop swaps connections StageTimer and audio with the A/V vendor
Notes: USB-C preferred; backup dongles for Dell Apple HP

Description: Give time warnings via StageTimer and never let the schedule run early
Notes: Keep Python trivia ready as filler

Description: Curate an ordered subset from the day's signup form and run the block
Notes: Saturday before close; Sunday around 4:45

Description: Request slides from speakers for posting and note no-share preferences
Notes: Respect speaker preferences

Description: Personally thank each speaker after their presentation
Notes: Small gesture that lands

Description: Thank all speakers in closing remarks and on social
Notes: Coordinate social posts with Marketing

Description: Email speakers for outstanding slides with a reasonable deadline
Notes: Follow up with stragglers and respect opt-outs

Description: Compile Slido and feedback-form data into a per-speaker feedback links doc and send it out
Notes: Speakers value seeing their own numbers and comments

Description: Check recording quality with the A/V vendor; the vendor delivers unlisted YouTube videos
Notes: Each video AND the playlist must be flipped public

Description: Survey speakers on their experience and what to improve
Notes: Feeds the retro

Description: Email speakers their published links and post on social with Marketing
Notes: Recordings also land on pyvideo.org via a manual PR

Description: Add this year's speakers to the per-year past-speaker Google Group
Notes: Feeds next year's direct CFP invitations

Description: Add lessons learned and update CFP questions KBYG and email templates
Notes: Knowledge transfer for future years

Description: Refresh the reviewer list for next year
Notes: Keep the review team strong

Description: Save this year's submissions and review data for future reference
Notes: Useful for trend analysis
